name: ʻEua National Park
coordinates_source: wikipedia:ʻEua National Park (infobox; park centre, check visitor point)
note: National park: Tonga's only forest national park (4.51 km²) on the east coast, a rainforest band above sea cliffs with caves and chasms; the hiking hub of ʻEua.

name: Big Ovava Tree
note: Natural landmark: a banyan-type tree said to be over 800 years old, the main attraction inside ʻEua National Park.

name: ʻEua National Park Coastal Walk
note: Hiking trail: coastal walk along the park's cliff tops with breathtaking ocean views, a day walk; pin at its midpoint once its route is found.

name: Matalanga ʻa Maui
note: Natural feature: a pothole said to date from the legendary Maui, named as a highlight of ʻEua.

name: Liʻangahuo ʻa Maui
coordinates_source: OSM viewpoint 'Li'anga Huo A Maui (Natural Archway)' (node 12464909371)
note: Natural arch: a stone land-bridge carved into the southern cliffs of ʻEua, reached by a short walk east from the Rock Gardens.

name: Rock Gardens
coordinates_source: Tonga Pocket Guide page geo tag (guidebook map pin)
note: Coastal landscape: clifftop rock outcrops on the south coast of ʻEua, about 30 minutes to explore, named as 'Rockgarden Cliffs' by the tourism board.

name: Lakufaʻanga Cliffs
coordinates_source: Tonga Pocket Guide page geo tag (guidebook map pin)
note: Cliff viewpoint: dramatic sea cliffs at the southern tip of ʻEua, with seabirds and the nearby Rock Gardens; a named highlight of the island.

name: Haʻaluma Beach
coordinates_source: Tonga Pocket Guide page geo tag (guidebook map pin)
note: Beach: small south-coast beach with large tidal pools for snorkelling and sunsets, reached by a steep sandy road; named as a swim stop by the tourism board.

name: ʻAna ʻAhu
note: Cave: one of ʻEua's extensive cave systems, known for stalactites and stalagmites; named in the tourism board's cave listing.

name: Cathedral Cave
coordinates_source: OSM cave_entrance Grand Cathedral cave and submarine cavern (node 6538601037)
note: Dive site: an underwater cavern about 30 m down, roughly 100 m long, with daylight through ceiling openings; the tourism board's 'one of the Pacific's largest underwater caverns' (name from a guide).

name: ʻOtumatafena Tidal Pools
coordinates_source: midpoint of the shore between Ohonua and Tufuvai (wikipedia centres; approximate, shore not in OSM as a named feature)
note: Coastal feature: a reef shore of small tidal pools close to sea level between ʻOhonua and Tufuvai, named as a highlight of ʻEua.

name: Tufuvai Beach
note: Beach: small beach at the village of Tufuvai on the west coast; visitor draw only as part of the shore with its tidal pools.

name: Ohonua
note: Town: the largest settlement and island capital of ʻEua, beside the only stream on the island; base for services on the west coast.

name: Tufuvai
note: Village: one of the original villages of ʻEua on the west coast, at the south end of the tidal shore.

name: Kalau
coordinates_source: OSM coastline way 22384947 Kalau (islet centre, approximate)
note: Islet: 35-acre islet 3.8 km south-west of ʻEua's southern tip; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Ha Unu Beach
note: Beach: named beach on the south-east coast of ʻEua in OpenStreetMap; no visitor source found naming it.

name: Kapa Beach
note: Beach: named beach on the south coast of ʻEua in OpenStreetMap; no visitor source found naming it.

name: Fangatave Beach
note: Beach: named beach on the south-east coast of ʻEua in OpenStreetMap, beside Fangatave Cliffs; no visitor source found naming it.

name: Ufilae Beach
note: Beach: named beach on the east coast of ʻEua in OpenStreetMap; no visitor source found naming it.

name: Fangatave Cliffs
